answer: In a decentralized agent trust network, each agent node acts as a graph vertex whose transaction edges carry stake-backed capacity. To prevent Sybil infiltration, the network audits mutual cross-attestation flows; if an attacker attempts to mirror legitimate topologies by spinning up cloned identities, their cut conductance collapses toward zero. Every candidate vertex must register through a verifiable delay cipher that binds hardware time to network participation, forcing an attacker to pay exponential compute overhead and forfeitable bonded collateral per puppet identity.
